title: The Resistance to Data Source Traceability: Inertia and Trust
text:
Despite rigorous academic proof of the necessity for complete data sourcing transparency in robust algorithmic bias detection, adoption often stalls due to organizational inertia. The complexity and cost associated with tracing every input variable back to its origin create powerful disincentives for existing systems.

Furthermore, cultural resistance rooted in proprietary secrecy contributes significantly to this gap. Stakeholders may fear that full transparency regarding data collection methods or inherent sampling limitations could expose competitive vulnerabilities or initiate challenging regulatory scrutiny. This perception often outweighs the measured risk of latent bias, prioritizing operational ease and institutional reputation over ethical certainty.
